CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with right elbow pain that began approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children (ages 13 and 10). He reports the pain is located at the tip/point of the elbow and is sharp in character, occurring with any movement. The pain radiates down the forearm. Patient recalls rough play during the game and was checked multiple times with a lacrosse stick by his 13-year-old son, which may have caused direct impact to the elbow. He denies a fall. Patient attempted treatment with Advil for a couple of days, which provided some relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Otherwise denies constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (previously known)

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays lacrosse with children. Family follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Patient reports good dietary compliance with salt restriction.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 150/90 (elevated, possibly white coat syndrome)
General: Well-appearing
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Cardiac: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known), otherwise normal
Right Elbow: Pain to palpation of the olecranon area on the posterior elbow, mild pain with flexion and extension, normal range of motion, mild swelling and bruising present

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: No fracture, no bony abnormality, normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion with mild swelling and bruising, likely secondary to direct lacrosse stick impact.
Plan: Ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling, ice three times daily for 20 minutes per session, avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow for healing.

Hypertension: Continue Lisinopril 20 mg daily. Blood pressure elevated today but may be related to white coat syndrome. Patient demonstrating good compliance with low salt diet.

Diabetes mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Blood glucose readings when checked range 80-100 mg/dL. Obtain A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment is needed in the future.
